bug_description.original: Heap-buffer-overflow in snmp_in_options OSS-Fuzz report: https://bugs.chromium.org/p/oss-fuzz/issues/detail?id=398067543 ``` Crash type: Heap-buffer-overflow READ 8 Crash state: snmp_in_options netsnmp_parse_args snmp_parse_args_fuzzer.c ```
bug_description.normalized: The staged testcase is decoded into a synthetic `argc`/`argv` command line that reaches Net-SNMP's `-I` input-option parsing. In `snmp_in_options`, suboption `S` requires a separate argument when no suffix follows the `S` character, but the vulnerable code fetches that argument with `cp = argv[optind++]` without first checking `optind < argc`. If no additional `argv` element remains, that statement reads one pointer past the heap-allocated `argv` array, matching the recorded ASan heap-buffer-overflow at `snmplib/mib.c:2396`.

source.description: First project statement on the vulnerable path that consumes the attacker-controlled command-line state by passing the crafted `-I` option string and the current `argc`/`argv` bounds into the helper that performs the out-of-bounds access.
source.value_from: Stage 01's reproduced run executed `snmp_parse_args_fuzzer` on the staged `poc`. The harness decoded those bytes into `argc` and a heap-allocated `argv` array, then called `snmp_parse_args(argc, argv, ss, "", NULL)`. This dispatch into `snmp_in_options` is the first project-code consumption of the crafted option string and argument-vector state that later drives the overflow.

root_cause.description: In the `case 'S'` fallback path, the helper consumes the next `argv` element without verifying that another element is still available. The fix adds exactly that missing `optind < argc` bounds check before indexing `argv`.
root_cause.note: `patch.diff` changes this line to `cp = optind < argc ? argv[optind++] : NULL;`, which directly identifies the missing obligation in the vulnerable source.

sink.description: Crash site. This statement performs the out-of-bounds read from the heap-allocated `argv` pointer array when the `S` suboption tries to consume a missing next argument.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports frame 0 `snmp_in_options /gt/_work/src/snmplib/mib.c:2396:22` with `READ of size 8` on address `0x502000000020`, exactly 0 bytes past the 16-byte `argv` allocation created by the harness.

parser_admitted.description: Sample-specific option-dispatch gate. The staged command line is admitted as a `-I` input-option argument, so execution enters the `case 'I'` handler and calls the vulnerable helper instead of stopping in getopt parsing.

tainted_value_origin.description: The harness decodes the staged testcase bytes into a heap-allocated `argv` array and corresponding `argc`, then passes that synthetic command line to Net-SNMP parsing.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The exact untrusted bytes are the staged file `gt_results/osv_ossfuzz_OSV-2025-162/poc`, executed in Stage 01's reproduced vulnerable run. The saved evidence shows those bytes produce the crashing `snmp_parse_args_fuzzer` invocation whose `argv` allocation is 16 bytes long, i.e. two pointer slots on the ASan run's 64-bit target.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness decodes the staged testcase into `argc` and a heap-allocated `argv` array, then calls `snmp_parse_args` on that synthetic command line.
`netsnmp_parse_args` reaches the `-I` option handler and passes the attacker-controlled input-option string plus the current `argc`/`argv` state to `snmp_in_options`.
`snmp_in_options` reaches suboption `S` with no inline suffix, falls back to consuming the next `argv` element without checking whether one remains, and reads past the end of the `argv` allocation.

fine_trace.note: Source. In the `case 'I'` handler, the parser passes the attacker-controlled `-I` payload together with the current `argc` and `argv` state into `snmp_in_options`, creating the project-side data that governs later `argv` consumption.

The helper iterates through the attacker-controlled `-I` suboptions until it reaches `S`. When `S` has no following inline characters, `!*(++cp)` is true and control selects the fallback path that will try to take the required `S` value from the next `argv` element instead.

Root cause and sink. On the fallback path from step 2, the helper reads the next `argv` slot without checking `optind < argc`, so a missing separate argument for `S` makes this statement step past the allocated `argv` array. ASan records the resulting 8-byte out-of-bounds read at this exact line, and the patch adds the missing precondition as `optind < argc ? argv[optind++] : NULL`.

cross_validation.sink_matches_crash: Yes. The saved ASan trace reports frame 0 `snmp_in_options /gt/_work/src/snmplib/mib.c:2396:22` with `READ of size 8`, which is exactly fine-trace step 3 and the top-level sink.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes. The runtime call stack `snmp_in_options -> netsnmp_parse_args -> LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` matches the fine trace's project flow from step 1 into step 3, with step 2 capturing the source-level control decision inside `snmp_in_options` that makes the out-of-bounds fetch reachable.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Yes. The staged testcase bytes become the synthetic `argc`/`argv` command line in the harness, step 1 passes that attacker-controlled state into Net-SNMP option parsing, step 2 selects the `S` fallback path from the crafted option string, and step 3 dereferences the same `argv` array out of bounds.

format.name: libFuzzer snmp_parse_args argv encoding
format.contract: The witness needs to decode, under `snmp_parse_args_fuzzer`, into an `argc`/`argv` layout where Net-SNMP option parsing reaches `case 'I'` and the `optarg` string reaches suboption `S` with no following inline characters, so `snmp_in_options` tries to obtain the required `S` argument from the next `argv` element. The saved source and runtime evidence support the narrower condition that no additional `argv` element remains for that required argument, causing `cp = argv[optind++]` to read past the allocated `argv` array for this staged `poc`; they do not prove a broader trigger class beyond that missing-next-argument state.

evidence_limitations: Stage 02 remained source-grounded and did not rerun the PoC or perform fixed-version differential validation; runtime evidence is limited to the saved reproduction report and sanitizer trace from Stage 01.

The saved artifacts do not record the exact numeric value of `optind` at the crashing iteration. The ground truth therefore anchors the bug to the source-proven missing `optind < argc` check and the observed out-of-bounds read, not to an uninstrumented exact equality relation.
